cases.name: Carol Ann Holmin Christensen
cases.about: She moved to Grays Harbor, Washington, in 1969 from Weippe, Idaho, where she grew up in Hoquiam in a large family. Carol was a registered member of the Blackfeet Tribe of Browning, MT. She was a young mother separated from her husband and determined to make it and worked as a waitress at Barn Door Tavern on Pacific Avenue South.
cases.narrative: On 5/8/1983 which was Mother's Day, her remains were found 6 days after she disappeared by a family hunting for mushrooms in a wooded section of Maple Valley, just off SE 244th Street and Hwy. 169. Her body had been dunked in water and reclothed backwards, she had one shoe on the wrong foot, the other shoe was not found. She had a paper bag placed over the head. Two cleaned fish were laid across her body. She had raw sausage around her, a wine bottle in her hand. In his confession before the court, he said he killed her sometime between May 2, 1983 through May 8, 1983.
